### Rulings that bind ###
- **R1** The verdict format is `wikiaudit/README.md` § sources.csv, verdicts.csv. Read it, and each scope claim's row
  in `claims_comlab.csv` and its line in the rule file (with the rule's `description`), before the first fetch. Append
  to `sources.csv` and `verdicts.csv`; change no existing row. Reuse an earlier source (`S001`-`S028`) when it holds
  the fact.
- **R2** Web access is firecrawl only (`C:/4DApp/.claude/skills/researching-web-with-firecrawl/SKILL.md`; never
  WebFetch or WebSearch). Set the key inside the same command, never print it or write it to a file:
  `export FIRECRAWL_API_KEY=$(tr -d '\r\n ' < C:/4DApp/_skills/researching-web-with-firecrawl/API.md) && C:/4DApp/.tools/firecrawl/node_modules/.bin/firecrawl scrape "<url>" -o labs/gaslab/audit_tasks/wikiaudit/sources/S<NNN>.md`
  (run from `C:/4DApp/repo`). A search needs `--sources web --json` (without it the CLI returns a tool catalogue, not
  web hits): `firecrawl search "<query>" --sources web --json -o labs/gaslab/audit_tasks/wikiaudit/search/<name>.json`.
  Read fetched files narrowly (`grep -n`).
- **R3** One `sources.csv` row per file you cite; a `sources/` file not cited by a verdict, and the `search/` folder,
  are deleted before you finish.
- **R4** A verdict goes on the root claim only (the scope ids). Each value is an evidence gate of a v2 rule: the rule
  gains weight when the reading passes the gate. Judge the gate's value and direction against the fault the rule names:
  - Fuel-trim claims (`CK0351`, `CK0441`, `CK0442`, `CK0444`, `CK0448`, `CK0516`, `CK0517`, `CK0520`, `CK0612`,
    `CK0613`, `CK0615`, `CK0619`, `CK0622`): the decisive facts are the healthy warm-idle STFT/LTFT band and the
    direction a lean or rich fault drives the trims. Prefer an OEM service text, a regulator or a trade training text.
  - Exhaust-gas claims (`CK0347`, `CK0348`, `CK0352`, `CK0355`, `CK0356`, `CK0358`, `CK0362`, `CK0367`, `CK0513`,
    `CK0514`, `CK0524`, `CK0527`, `CK0528`): the decisive facts are the four- or five-gas signature of the named fault
    at warm idle (a misfire raises HC and O2 together; a dead or overwhelmed catalyst passes HC, CO and NOx and lowers
    CO2), and the healthy values with a working catalyst.
  - Other claims (`CK0611` Brettschneider λ < 0.97 for rich; `CK0445` MAP < 40 kPa; `CK0447` MAF < 3.5 g/s): the rich
    λ boundary, the warm-idle manifold absolute pressure of a healthy petrol engine, and the warm-idle mass airflow.
  - Verdicts: the source names the value, or a value inside 20 % of it, as the boundary in the same direction →
    `CONFIRMED`; the gate sits inside the source's healthy band (it fires on healthy readings) or points the wrong
    way → `CONTRADICTED`, with the healthy band in `source_value`; the source supports the direction but gives a
    boundary more than 20 % away → `PARTLY`; no fetched source decides it after three searches → `UNSOURCED`.
- **R5** Source kinds per `wikiaudit/README.md`. A paywalled standard (SAE, ISO, OIML) counts by its abstract or
  scope page as `PRIMARY_STANDARD`; a regulator's text is `PRIMARY_REGULATOR` or `PRIMARY_LAW`; a sensor maker or
  vehicle maker is `OEM`; trade training and analyser makers are `TRADE`; Wikipedia and forums are `SECONDARY`. A
  verdict from a `SECONDARY` or `TRADE` source says so in `note`. When a source contradicts your own knowledge, or two
  sources disagree, write both in `note` and pick the verdict the stronger text supports; list each such case in the
  progress note under `Disputes`.
- **R6** CSVs are UTF-8 as written; the checker rejects double-encoded fields.
